next.reason: CHANGED on item c alone (family ruling, difference 1). 1985: 'If the AT END phrase is not specified, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1, and that procedure is executed' (§1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR10), and a READ with neither is refused: 'The INVALID KEY phrase or the AT END phrase must be specified if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is specified for file-name-1' (§1985:VIII.4.5.3 SR5). 2023: 'any applicable at end exception processing statements are executed. If there are no applicable at end exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the READ statement' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24), and 14.9.30.3 has no rule that requires either. The words that differ are 'must be associated' against 'If there are no applicable': a case added, so 2023 accepts and defines a READ that 1985 refuses. The three triggers are carried: no next record and the absent optional file ('If the file position indicator indicates that an optional input file is not present or that no next or previous logical record exists', §2023:14.9.30.4 GR21; §2023:9.1.13.4 GR1), and the one this rule's own text adds to its sequential sibling, 'the number of significant digits in the relative record number is larger than the size of the relative key data item' (§1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR10), which 2023 states as 'the I-O status value associated with file-name-1 is set to '14', the at end condition exists' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR21) with the value of §2023:9.1.13.4 GR2; that case is why this record lists GR-9.1.13.4-2 and VII.4.4.4 GR10 does not. 1985's 'A value, derived from the setting of the file position indicator' is those two values. The rest is carried and is no ground. AT END comes first, with 'Any other applicable exception processing statements are not executed' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24) for 1985's 'Any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is not executed'. The USE declarative is the applicable exception processing statement ('Statements in a file-exception or exception-name format of a USE declarative', §2023:9.1.12 GR2), run 'unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR6), and 1985's 'Return from that procedure is to the next executable statement following the end of the READ statement' is 'control is returned to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR7). 'When the at end condition exists, execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24). GR24's 'if enabled, the EC-I-O-AT-END exception condition is set to exist' is reached only through exception checking 1985 has no syntax to enable, and under the family ruling is no ground. Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993) reworded b and c and kept the obligation of c. The record operation conflict proviso of §2023:14.9.30.4 GR13 belongs to the sibling rule GR11, not to this one.
